author: Emily Prescott
title: Mamdani's Remarks on Private Property Draw Backlash - NewsBreak
text: New York City Democratic nominee for mayor Zohran Mamdani has faced growing criticism after a resurfaced video showed him expressing support for abolishing private property. In the footage, Mamdani argued that private ownership perpetuates inequality. Republicans have labeled the stance as radical and a threat to economic security. Mamdani has become an increasingly controversial political figure, as most analysts expect him to secure a victory in the November general election. Mamdani stated that if there was any system that could guarantee each person housing—whether it’s the abolition of private property or a statewide housing guarantee—it is preferable to what is going on right now. Mamdani added that people try to play gotcha games about these kinds of things, but he cares more about whether someone has a home. In the video, Mamdani advocates for guaranteed housing, suggesting abolishing private property or creating a statewide housing guarantee. Reps. Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY) and Mike Lawler (R-NY) criticized the remarks as communist. Malliotakis stated that he claims to be a socialist, whether wanting to abolish private property or seize the means of production; these ideas are right out of Karl Marx’s playbook. Malliotakis added that the willingness of too many media members and the Democrat Party to go along instead of calling him out is disturbing. She believes that if the majority of New Yorkers knew what Mamdani truly stands for and how destructive his policies are, there’s no way they would vote for him, as many in the city have lived in places where socialism and communism destroyed lives. Rep. Claudia Tenney (R-NY) warned that abolishing private property would hurt families, small businesses, and community stability. Mamdani has proposed building 200,000 affordable housing units funded by higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations. Tenney stated that Mamdani’s call to abolish private property isn’t just radical, it’s dangerous. She explained that stripping this fundamental right would devastate families, close small businesses, and destroy entire communities while handing more power to the government. Tenney added that private property is a cornerstone constitutional principle representing personal freedom, economic opportunity, and the American Dream, and that it must be defended. Mamdani will face Mayor Eric Adams, GOP nominee Curtis Sliwa, and independent former Gov. Andrew Cuomo in the general election. He failed to secure endorsements from top Democrats like Gov. Kathy Hochul or Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY). Emily Prescott covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
